To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

heterologous anti lymphocyte serum can be prepared that is demonstrable by immunofluoroscent techniques as having both in vitro and in vivo anti glomerular antibody activity, that this activity can be demonstrated in the kidney of a dog, and that this activity can cause early glomerular injury.

the potential nephro-toxicity of hetero-lymphocyte sera was investigated in dogs; horse anti-dog lymph-node serum was demonstrated to possess both in vitro and in vivo anti-glomerular activity; and while none of the animals treated with the serum subcutaneously or by the intravenous route showed clinical evidence of renal injury, early histological changes of glomerular disease were apparent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible nephrotoxic effects of anti-lymphocytic sera.
the potential nephro-toxic effects of anti-lymphocytic serum.
the development of anti-lymphocytic sera which are free of nephrotoxic activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while there is a potential nephrotoxin in horse anti-dog lymph node cell anti-lymphocytic serum, the risk of its expression in the dog is small.
, in this experimental model, the administration of hetero-antiserum to the host did not produce a nephritis.
, under the experimental conditions employed in this investigation, the administration of horse anti-lymphocytic serum to dogs did not induce a serum sickness type nephritis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the administration of horse anti-dog lymphocytes serum does not cause nephrotoxic serum disease in dogs.

, while heterologous anti-dog lymphocytes serum does possess the potential for causing a nephritis of the type seen in the experimental model, this is not a likely consequence of its administration in the doses and routes used for the treatment of human disease.

, at least in dogs, anti-lymphocytic serum is not nephrotoxic.
